question: Does the DEM dissipation path reproduce collective inelastic cooling of a dilute granular gas (Haff's law) and the Boltzmann cooling coefficient, not just the single-impact restitution?

external_anchors.claim: theta(t) = theta0 (1+t/tau)^-2, exponent -2, theta^-1/2 linear in t
dilute inelastic hard-sphere cooling rate from collision frequency x energy loss

external_anchors.ref: Enskog collision frequency (3-D): omega = 24 phi g0 sqrt(theta/pi)/sigma
external_anchors.claim: anchor used to validate the collision-frequency branch of the derivation

A5_rest_scaling_rel.metric: spread of K_meas/(1-e_eff^2) over the e sweep

A7_elastic_energy_drift.metric: range of total mechanical energy / E0 at e=1

notes: Prefactor test uses the measured e_eff (clamped spring-dashpot bias), never the nominal restitution. Frictionless and monodisperse by design so the model and the Boltzmann prediction are structurally comparable. Absolute 3% agreement is NOT claimed a priori: finite-density velocity correlations are a known correction; the phi->0 extrapolation (A4) is the fair test of the prefactor.
